description: The Pilot Overview dashboard is similar to the general Continuous Monitoring Air Quality Overviews, but with the filter and limitation already applied for the specific pilot location. On it all the aggregated measurements are available in a single common panel and, since the data scope is limited, it can be used as a pilot's main page when limit access to users to that scope is needed and the general one is not offered to avoid access to other pilots’ data. Furthermore, this allows to potentially differentiate the specific pilots overview panels if some aspects or information shown needs to be customized. As in the general one, this view allows the comparison of all of the measurements aggregated, which allow global exports, but its filtering via top filters or selection in the legend will generally be necessary for practical use.

options.content:
Spain Pilot Overview
Barcelona pilot study covers the two approaches proposed by K-HEALTHinAIR:
  1. Follow up of high-risk multimorbid outpatients with obstructive lung disease:
    The work with the outpatients is focused on analyzing the relationships between patient’s home Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) and health status, with focus on acute health effects. It includes the collection of health-related data such as medical surveillance, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMS), Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMS), standardized health questionnaires, and the monitoring of biological signals such as heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV) and activity indicators (steps and calories). Also, the study considers the monitoring of relevant parameters, Temperature (T), Relative Humidity (RH), CO2 concentration / sensor (CO2), Particle matter (PM), Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) and formaldehyde, in their homes (the indoor environment where they spend a mayor part of their lives) and the sampling of the key health affecting agents: PM, VOCs (including formaldehyde) and microbiome in some selected outpatients the IAQ of their homes.
  2. Analysis of 3 relevant settings, hospital areas, metro station and a market:
    The work with the settings, hospital, metro station and market, is focused on monitoring of the relevant parameters, T, RH, CO2, PM, VOCs and formaldehyde, the sampling of the key health affecting agents: PM, VOCs (including formaldehyde) and microbiome in the IAQ, the collection of OAQ in the surrounding areas and the use of questionnaires with the staff (because in principle this is the population group spending more time inside these settings).
Spain Pilot description.
More info about manipulating pannels in the Home screen

panels.description: This is the main, basic dashboard for the Spain Pilot. Filtering by type of indoor scenario, specific scenario building, area, sensor device, indoor or outdoor air quality data and also pollutant is possible. Dashed lines are outdoor air quality data and each individual type of pollutant has its own color in the graph.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "AIR_QUALITY")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "CONTINUOUS_MONITORING_")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.id_pilot == "ES")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.AQ =~ /^${aq:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.scenario =~ /^${scenario:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sub_scenario =~ /^${sub_scenario:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.area =~ /^${area:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.sensor_id =~ /^${sensor_id:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field =~ /^${pollutant:regex}$/)

list.definition:
from(bucket: "AIR_QUALITY")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "CONTINUOUS_MONITORING_")
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>  r.id_pilot == "ES")
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>  r.scenario =~ /^${scenario:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["sub_scenario"])
  |> distinct(column: "sub_scenario")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])
